newsitem.title: USA: PGE to supply Palm Springs, Calif., power.
newsitem.headline: PGE to supply Palm Springs, Calif., power.

text.p: The city of Palm Springs, Calif., will announce later today it has selected Portland General Electric Co to supply its power needs starting in 1998, a city consultant said Thursday.
The Oregon utility, which is being acquired by Enron Corp, was chosen over competitor Illinova Power Marketing due its more attractive proposal and "forward thinking," said Arthur Lyons.

Lyons helped spearhead a bid by the desert community to circumvent current provider Southern California Edison Co, but that move was turned down by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission earlier this year.
Lyons noted the municipality will still be able to aggregate retail loads under California's restructuring law, which will be phased in starting in 1998.
SoCal Edison, the main subsidiary of Edison International, will compete with Portland General to supply retail buyers within the city's limits.
Palm Springs expects to conclude a municipal service agreement with PGE shortly, after which details of load volumes will be worked out, Lyons said.
He noted that the Oregon utility has guaranteed prices below Edison's, although the city will still have to pay "competitive transition charges", or CTCs, as mandated by the state law.
The CTCs represent the cost of utility investments expected to become uneconomic under market competition.
The state's Public Utilities Commission has not yet determined a CTC for Edison's territory, but last week set a 39.2 percent of rates for customers of San Francisco-based Pacific Gas and Electric.
Lyons said PGE's proposal to Palm Springs included an estimated CTC of 4.4 cents per kilowatt hour - a level which would exceed the Pacific Gas and Electric rate.
